About this system

Browser-only Filipino Sign Language recognition, including the ASL-based A–Z manual alphabet for fingerspelling, using hand landmarks and local KNN classification.

Recognition support--

About recognition and privacy

A pretrained ASL-based A–Z hand-landmark model estimates fingerspelling letters locally in this browser; J/Z can also be traced as motions. It is an alphabet model, not a full FSL vocabulary model, and has not been validated with diverse FSL signers. Other FSL signs can use browser-local trained KNN samples. Webcam frames are not uploaded and no application backend is used.

Gather approved sign samples

Choose an FSL sign or alphabet letter, connect the camera, and capture varied, correctly labeled examples. Samples stay on this device.

Common phrase labels and Ñ are not pre-trained. Capture at least 3 separate, approved samples per sign or letter, then train KNN to recognize them.

More about samples and model limits

The bundled pretrained model recognizes static A–Z handshapes only; it does not recognize common FSL words. Common signs default to Dynamic mode; verify the correct sign type against an FSL reference, then capture at least 3 separate, correctly labeled performances per sign and use Trained KNN. Use Capture one once per separate static attempt; adjacent video frames from one held pose are not independent examples. Static letters use Static mode, except J/Z. The model runs locally and is licensed CC BY-NC 4.0; see its attribution and license in the models folder.

Build your translation

Recognized signs can be added to your text and spoken aloud. Adjust recognition and voice settings below.

The pretrained alphabet model runs locally; Trained KNN uses samples saved in this browser.

Filipino mode prefers an installed Filipino or Tagalog voice, including Ñ as “enye.” If unavailable, it uses an English (Philippines) or English (US) voice. Voice availability depends on your browser and device.
